A speeding hit-and-run driver killed a 28-year-old nurse walking home from working the overnight shift at a  nearby Brooklyn hospital on Saturday, according to officials and video of the crash.

Jiayi Zheng — still wearing her forest green scrubs — was walking along the crosswalk at 55th Street and Third Avenue when the operator of a black Cadillac sedan drove through a red light and barreled into her around 7:30 a.m. in Sunset Park, disturbing footage shows.

Zheng was sent flying in the air before landing on the median, just a block away from where she worked at NYU Langone-Brooklyn Hospital as a medical- surgical unit nurse.

Medics rushed her to the same hospital, but she succumbed to her head and neck injuries.

Topic:Social Media

New videos of people committing crimes continue to emerge on social media, as the government tries to stop them.

Experts say the videos and media commentary about them are driving a sense of notoriety among those committing crimes.

The WA government is trying to pass laws that would criminalise posting and boasting about crimes online, but legal experts have raised concerns.

"Crimfluencer" videos on social media appearing to depict young people in Western Australia's far north joy-riding in stolen cars are continuing to gain popularity as the government wrestles with the problem of how to stop it.

The term "crimfluencer" has emerged among academics and politicians alike to describe people who use social media to gain notoriety or a following by glorifying criminal behaviour.
